title: The Koszul chain complex is a projective resolution of its quotient
statement: For every commutative ring A, ideal I, natural number r, and sequence f:Fin r -> A which is Koszul-regular [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence] and has span(range f)=I, there exists a projective resolution P of the A-module A/I whose chain complex is exactly K_A(f) [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex]. No assumption that I is proper or r is positive is made.

source.place: Lemma 48.15.5, finite free Koszul resolution; Tags 0623 and 062E for the augmentation and Koszul regularity

proof.text: Identify the degree-one differential with Finsupp.linearCombination A f under exteriorPower.oneEquiv and exteriorPower.zeroEquiv, by exteriorPower.linearMap_ext and CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft_ι. Its range is I by Finsupp.range_linearCombination and hf. Define q as I.mkQ after zeroEquiv and prove d_1 followed by q is zero. ChainComplex.toSingle₀Equiv constructs the augmentation to the quotient concentrated in degree zero.

The quotient map q is surjective, and its kernel equals the image of d_1: lift an element of I along linearCombination, then along oneEquiv. ShortComplex.moduleCat_exact_iff proves exactness, so hex.gIsCokernel identifies the quotient with the opcycles. Use ChainComplex.quasiIsoAt₀_iff and ShortComplex.quasiIso_iff_isIso_descOpcycles to prove degree-zero quasi-isomorphism by this cokernel isomorphism. In every other degree, hreg and exactAt_iff_isZero_homology give source exactness, while exactAt_single_obj gives target exactness; quasiIsoAt_iff_exactAt completes the proof.

For every n, apply ModuleCat.projective_of_free to the basis (Finsupp.basisSingleOne).exteriorPower n of the term wedge^n(A^r). Bundle K, these projectivity proofs, the constructed augmentation, and its quasi-isomorphism into ProjectiveResolution. The complex field equality is rfl; no choice of an arbitrary resolution or change of complex is involved.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 48.15.5, local finite free Koszul resolution; Tags 0623 and 062E. J4 adapts the already proved augmentation argument of Sheaf.RingTheory.KoszulRegularSequenceDualComplex directly to the natural-number chain complex because that module imports this item transitively. Projectivity uses Mathlib ModuleCat.projective_of_free and Module.Basis.exteriorPower.

from.place: The Koszul chain complex is a projective resolution of its quotient

lean.statement: theorem exists_koszul_projective_resolution (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) (hreg : RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f) (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) : ∃ P : ProjectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I)), P.complex = koszulComplex A r f
